ticker: Delhi ranks as world's most polluted major city on Diwali eve.
Israeli President taps Gadi Eisenkot to form new government.
US military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce and blockades.
At least six killed in shocking mass shooting incident in Krakow.
Bangladesh's Towhid Hridoy hits historic double century against West Indies.

articles.headline: Delhi Ranked World's Most Polluted Major City
articles.brief: Delhi has been named the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali by a Swiss group, sparking fresh concerns over air quality as officials urge citizens to adopt greener celebration methods and minimize harmful emissions.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot Tapped to Form Israeli Government
articles.brief: Israeli President has selected former military chief and Netanyahu rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form a new government following ongoing political shifts and negotiations within the parliament.

articles.headline: US Military Targets Iranian Land Commerce
articles.brief: Expanding beyond traditional naval blockades, the US military is reportedly looking into new strategies to restrict Iranian land commerce to counter regional threats and economic flows.

articles.headline: Berkshire Hathaway Speeds Up Stock Buybacks
articles.brief: Berkshire Hathaway has accelerated its stock buyback initiatives despite reporting a general fall in overall corporate profits during the latest quarter, according to financial disclosures.

articles.headline: Mass Shooting in Krakow Leaves Six Dead
articles.brief: Poland is in a state of shock after at least six people were killed following a tragic mass shooting incident in the popular tourist hotspot of Krakow, prompting heightened security measures.

articles.headline: Microsoft Winds Down Oracle Cloud AI Deal
articles.brief: Microsoft is reportedly winding down an existing agreement with Oracle to rent cloud capacity for artificial intelligence operations, shifting focus toward internal infrastructure developments.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola India Bottler Files For IPO
articles.brief: Hindustan Coca-Cola, the major bottling arm of Coca-Cola in India, has officially filed preliminary paperwork to launch an initial public offering in the country.

articles.headline: Towhid Hridoy Hits Record Double Century
articles.brief: Towhid Hridoy made history for Bangladesh by scoring a record-breaking double century during the second Test match against the West Indies, surpassing previous national batting milestones.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Upholds Somnath Temple Food Ban
articles.brief: The Supreme Court has refused to lift restrictions on non-vegetarian food sales near the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, instructing the local High Court to address challenges swiftly.

articles.headline: TSMC Considers Advanced Memory Chip Production
articles.brief: Semiconductor manufacturing giant TSMC is reportedly exploring options to expand its portfolio by producing advanced memory chips to meet rising global technological demand.

articles.headline: FSSAI Suspends Over One Thousand Licences
articles.brief: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has suspended 1,133 licences nationwide following extensive inspections and a massive crackdown on food safety violations.

articles.headline: EPFO Expects 25 Percent Contribution Surge
articles.brief: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation anticipates a twenty-five percent increase in total contributions by fiscal year 2027-2028 following upcoming wage ceiling adjustments.

articles.headline: Trump Proposes Dana White for Press Secretary
articles.brief: Former US President Donald Trump has suggested that UFC chief executive Dana White would make an ideal White House press secretary in future political campaigns.

articles.headline: Hardik Pandya Traded to Punjab Kings
articles.brief: In a major upcoming Indian Premier League development, star cricketer Hardik Pandya is set to move to Punjab Kings in exchange for fast bowler Arshdeep Singh.

articles.headline: China Expands Mining Footprint in Africa
articles.brief: China is aggressively tightening its control over critical global minerals with a massive $16 billion mining investment push across Africa amid rising geopolitical rivalry with the United States.
